newsitem.title: USA: Daschle supports investing Social Security funds.
newsitem.headline: Daschle supports investing Social Security funds.

text.p: Senate Democratic Leader Tom Daschle said Tuesday he would support a pilot project for investing Social Security funds in the stock market. But he said he would oppose individual private investments using Social Security funds.

"My view is that the (Social Security) trust fund itself ought to experiment in private investment with a pilot project allocating a certain percentage of its resouces in the market to afford us an opportunity to compare both the security as well as the return on investments," Daschle told reporters.

Several members of a federal advisory panel on Monday recommended investing some of the Social Security trust funds in the stock market, but the panel could not reach overall agreement on how to keep the fund solvent into the next century.
Without change, the fund could be depleted by 2030 as millions of Americans retire.

Currently, Social Security funds can be invested only in Treasury securities, which provide a lower rate of return than the private market. Estimates are that shifting into market-based funds could increase the program's rate of return to 4.2 percent from the current 2.3 percent.
